label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss) is alert-FP because user input flows through encodeForHTML() before reaching the response writer, which properly sanitizes HTML special characters. Alert 2 (java/path-injection) is alert-TP because fileTarget is constructed directly from user-controlled input (param from request headers) without validation, allowing path traversal/enumeration attacks. The case-level label is TP because at least one alert (path-injection) represents a genuine vulnerability.

evidence.note: User input extracted from request headers into param variable
Switch statement assigns user-controlled param to bar variable (case C matches switchTarget='C')
File constructed from bar (user input) - path injection vulnerability
Response output uses encodeForHTML() to sanitize fileTarget.toString(), mitigating XSS
